title: Rapid model rollback — all-hands prep & comm scratch
body:
Purpose: scratchpad to assemble a short, pragmatic all-hands/engineer-facing comms bundle for a rapid model rollback scenario. Not polished; collection of proposed lines, Qs, numbers to surface.

Context (quick):
- Yesterday ~10:40 UTC we deployed quant-v2 for hosted endpoints behind a canary. Over the next hour we saw a subtle drift in answer quality for high-temperature completions (customer reports + internal evals). By 13:10 UTC error/garbled output rate increased for certain prefix classes.
- Rollback decision: partial rollback to quant-v1 across the affected pool at 14:05 UTC. A rolling fallback was in place as stopgap. This doc is to prepare the all-hands segment, quick Q&A, and slack templates.

Audience: engineers (all teams), product owners, support, SRE, and execs who will be on call for the next 24–72h. Keep tone: factual, accountable, next-steps oriented, no finger-pointing.

Key metrics to surface (what people will ask):
- % of requests affected: approx 6.8% of served requests in canary pool (13:00–14:00 UTC)
- Error/quality signal: human-eval fail rate on 200-sample threshold tests spiked from 4.2% -> 18.9% for targeted prompts
- Latency/cost: negligible change due to rollback (same instance sizes)
- Customer impact: 3 active PMs reported anomalies in customer QA; none escalated to legal or security.

Proposed 90s CEO/lead talking points (concise):
- "We prioritized correctness and user trust: when early signals pointed to a quality regression during a canary, we rolled back quickly to the verified variant and launched a focused investigation.
- We will finish a root-cause analysis within 3 business days and share a remediation plan with teams.
- Short term: engineers can expect additional guarding around canary evaluation thresholds and more conservative canary width by default."

Engineer-facing quick bullet script (30–60s):
- What happened: "A new quantized variant showed regressions on a small set of prompts in canary. We rolled back the variant in the affected pool at 14:05 UTC. Serving has returned to baseline for those routes."
- Why it mattered: "Quality regressions can silently degrade product experiences. Canary evals caught this early. Rolling back reduces blast radius while we investigate."
- Immediate ask: "If you maintain endpoints with custom prompt templates, please run your key prompt smoke tests on staging and paste failures in #ops-rollback with the "rollback-2025-02-14" tag."

Suggested all-hands slide bullets (single slide):
- Timeline (deploy -> detection -> rollback) with UTC timestamps
- Impact: approx 7% of requests in canary; no data exfiltration, no SLA breach
- Next steps: RCA + mitigation plan in 72h; short policy tweaks for future canaries
- Who to contact: Aisha (canary metrics), Rowan (rollback ops), Dev oncall (pager rotation)

Q&A (anticipated) + short answers:
- Q: "Why did the regression happen if the model passed unit tests?"
  A: "Unit tests covered functional correctness and perf, but this variant reveals distributional sensitivity on certain prompt patterns; our canary tests caught that gap."
- Q: "Was customer data exposed or compromised?"
  A: "No — this was a quality regression, not a security incident. We found no evidence of data leakage."
- Q: "Will rollbacks become more frequent?"
  A: "No — we will tighten canary thresholds and add a small eval suite using representative customer prompts to reduce false negatives."
- Q: "Can we auto-fallback if a variant degrades?"
  A: "Yes — follow-up work: implement automated rollback triggers based on eval/test delta. Short term we rely on manual rollback for high-risk variants."

Operational checklist to run in next 24 hours (owner in parens):
- Confirm rollback fully propagated & monitor (Rowan)
- Expand sample set for the RCA to include customer prompt classes (Aisha + solutions eng)
- Postmortem skeleton (template) + notify support with canned responses (Marta)
- Lock down deploys for the affected model family for 48h (release-engineering)
- Draft public-safe customer note if key customers ask (customer-success)

Slack / in-product message templates (short):
- Internal #platform-ops: "Heads-up: rolled back quant-v2 -> quant-v1 for affected pool at 14:05 UTC due to quality regression in canary. Monitoring closely. Tag: rollback-2025-02-14"
- Support reply skeleton: "We observed anomalous model outputs for a small set of requests and reverted to the previously verified model variant. If you continue to see issues please share an example and we will prioritize investigation."

Open questions / TBD (for the postmortem):
- Exact prompt classes that triggered the regression — need more labeled examples from customers.
- Telemetry gaps: can we automatically snapshot failing inferences to a secure triage store (privacy review required)?
- Threshold tuning: what are safe default deltas for automatic canary rejection? (metric owner: Aisha)

Draft delivery plan for all-hands (timeline):
- T0 (ASAP): Ping execs + eng managers with brief (done)
- T+1h: short slide + CEO 90s script ready (this doc)
- T+2h: run mini-demo in staging showing pre/post outputs for 3 representative prompts (Rowan)
- T+24–72h: postmortem + action items published on Confluence; follow-ups in next weekly eng sync

Notes to self:
- Keep the language focused on mitigation and learning. Avoid technical deep-dives in the first update.
- Collect 6–8 anonymized prompt examples we can show internally (privacy scrub first).
- Flag any legal/customer escalation early to the exec office.

Todos (short):
- [ ] Finalize CEO lines and run through with comms (Nikhil)
- [ ] Prepare 1-slide timeline (Rowan)
- [ ] Populate postmortem template (Marta)
- [ ] Post internal note to #all-hands at 16:00 UTC (Aisha)

End of scratch — will iterate and move to Confluence once cleaned up.
